listing.name: Fallout (Fallout Community Edition)
listing.summary: Windows prepared-player route: use Fallout Community Edition1.1.0 in a permitted complete original Fallout installation. Preserve actual working directory, fallout.cfg, original DAT/patch/music paths and save roots. Upstream owns preparation and replacement; Core offers nonowning registration/Play, without granting original rights or managed save compatibility.

steps.title: Use the actual Community Edition player
steps.instruction: Keep a complete already permitted Fallout Community Edition1.1.0 Windows x64 copy and its supported original Fallout installation. Upstream documents fallout-ce.exe as the drop-in player in that game folder. Select it directly, not the original DOS/Windows executable, installer or another mod engine. Native Windows entry runs the game in the selected process; it uses the shared GNW95MUTEX and can decline to start when another such instance exists.

steps.title: Prepare original data outside Core
steps.instruction: Finish the upstream setup using your own complete supported original game installation, with original master.dat/critter.dat, patch/data/music and all other necessary files. Keep the whole creating runtime/data tuple rather than reconstruct a guessed minimal folder. Start/quit upstream normally before registration. Core neither imports nor authenticates those originals or private outputs.

steps.title: Preserve the established working directory and config
steps.instruction: Select the actual game folder as working directory and preserve supported existing literal arguments. Windows entry does not change directory for you. fallout.cfg is located using the executable path; actual master/critter DAT, patch and music locations can be relative or custom absolute paths. Keep the exact established paths rather than rewriting a host root or forcing a new portable profile. Review consent and choose Play separately.

steps.title: Keep all actual save and data roots
steps.instruction: Preserve the complete external runtime/original data, fallout.cfg, actual master_patches/data root including SAVEGAME and slot contents, music, mods, screenshots/logs and unknown files. Retain every configured external root and old creating copy; another executable directory alone does not prove save or instance isolation. No arbitrary Fallout mod or cross-version save compatibility is established.

steps.title: Keep the separate license and asset boundaries
steps.instruction: The selected engine uses Sustainable Use License1.0, not GPL/MIT. Its personal/noncommercial/internal-business scope, free noncommercial distribution conditions and notices remain applicable. This guide adds no general commercial, original-asset, mod, repackaging or redistribution grant; attach only a copy you are already permitted to use.

steps.title: Keep replacement and removal ownership clear
steps.instruction: Close all real instances before external file changes. Upstream/player owns preparation, runtime replacement, profile writes and any migration/recovery. Preserve the old creating copy and every actual data root, finish deliberate replacement upstream and review/relink the changed player before the next Play. Core observes only its separately consented selected process, not an exclusive instance family or sandbox, and does not adopt unrelated helpers/successors. Registration-only removal preserves all external files. No Core-managed acquisition/setup/update/backup/rollback/migration/deletion is offered by this route.

warnings: This guide adds no Supported promotion, original/component permission, acquired-source-to-binary or private-output certificate. Use only a copy and content you are already permitted to use.
Source/API and inert native probes are distinct from actual game/save/mod/network, installed Desktop, physical/human, other-platform or protected acceptance. No such new observation is claimed.
Keep complete actual external runtime and player-data roots recoverable before upstream changes; another player folder does not guarantee independent shared state.
